Smt. Nisha Devi And Another vs State Of U.P. on 21 February,
2023
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?Court No. - 85
Case :- Criminal Misc Anticipatory Bail Application U/S 438 Cr.P.C. No. - 13047 of 2022
Applicant :- Smt. Nisha Devi And Another

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Shiv Lal,Manvendra Narain Pathak,P.K. Singh

Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Dhirendra Kumar Dwivedi
Hon'ble Mrs. Jyotsna Sharma,J.
1.
Counter affidavit filed by the first informant today is taken on record.

2. Heard Sri P.K. Singh, learned counsel for the applicants, Sri Dhirendra Kumar Dwivedi, learned counsel for the first informant, Sri O.P. Mishra, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.

3. The instant anticipatory bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicants with a prayer to release them on anticipatory bail in Case Crime No. 0254 of 2020, under Sections 419, 420, 120-B IPC, Police Station Meja, District Prayagraj.

4. As per prosecution case, the applicants fraudulently bought land being portion of plot no. 1201 from Shrawan Kumar and Veer Pratap; it is alleged in the FIR that the aforesaid Shrawan Kumar and Veer Pratap managed to get their name wrongly recorded in revenue papers with regard to land belonging to Kiran Devi; thereafter in a fraudulent transaction, same was transferred in favour of present applicants Smt. Nisha Devi and Raj Kumar by execution of a registered sale deed dated 18.04.2019.

5. It is contended on behalf of the applicants that they purchased the land from recorded owners; it is contended that the first informant in fact owned a portion of the land of the same plot and it never happened that they purchased her portion; it is further argued that the case at the most entails a Smt. entities.text: Nisha Devi And Another vs State Of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 1 civil remedy; in fact Kiran Devi-the first informant has already filed a suit for cancellation of two sale deeds and a civil cases are pending; the applicants are having no criminal antecedents; in case the sale deeds are found not valid, they shall suffer; they are in fact the bonafide purchasers.

6. The application for anticipatory bail is opposed by the other side pressing before me the facts that the applicants entered into a sham transactions to grab the land belonging to the first informant in pursuance of a deep conspiracy hatched by them in collusion with the sellers.
However, the broader contours of the matter could not be denied.

7. In case of Siddharam Satlingappa Mhetre v. State of Maharashtra, (2011) 1 SCC 694, it has been held by the Supreme Court that while deciding anticipatory bail, Court must consider nature and gravity of accusation, antecedent of accused, possibility of accused to flee from justice and that Court must evaluate entire available material against the accused carefully and that the exact role of the accused has also to be taken into consideration.

entities.text: Siddharam Satlingappa Mhetre v. State of Maharashtra, (2011) 1 SCC 694
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 8. In the instant case, I considered submissions of the learned counsel for the parties, nature of accusation, role of applicants and all attending facts and circumstances of the case.
In my view, a case for anticipatory bail is made out.
In case of breach of any of the above conditions, the court below shall have the liberty to cancel the bail granted to the applicants.
